vendors.name: Bentley Systems
vendors.tagline: Infrastructure engineering software (STAAD.Pro, OpenRoads, ProjectWise)
vendors.market_position: Bentley Systems makes engineering software for infrastructure, including STAAD.Pro for structural design, OpenRoads Designer for roads, MicroStation for CAD and ProjectWise for project delivery. It publishes USD prices for 12-month Virtuoso subscriptions on its website, with enterprise licensing by quote. Bentley lists no Oman office; its nearest offices are in Dubai and Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia.
pros: Published prices for single licences (USD, 12-month subscriptions)
Structural, road and CAD design tools from one vendor
ProjectWise for shared project documents and delivery
Oman's OQ won a Bentley Going Digital Award in 2022 (Times of Oman)
cons: Engineering design software, not site admin or accounting
No Oman office or confirmed Oman partner
Annual per-user subscriptions paid upfront
Specialist tools with a learning curve for each discipline
vendors.typical_pricing: Published on bentley.com in USD, per 12-month Virtuoso subscription for one licence: STAAD.Pro from $3,995, STAAD.Pro Advanced from $5,490, Structural WorkSuite from $6,097, Bentley Infrastructure Cloud Connect from $312 and ProjectWise from $960. ProjectWise Bundle from $10,440. Enterprise licensing by quote.
vendors.om_specific_note: Most relevant to structural, road and utility design work rather than general contracting or bookkeeping. Times of Oman reported in December 2022 that OQ won one of Bentley's Going Digital Awards in Infrastructure. Bentley lists no Oman office, so ask who supports it locally before you buy.

vendors.name: Oracle Primavera P6
vendors.tagline: Oracle's critical-path scheduling and project portfolio software
vendors.market_position: Primavera P6 is Oracle's project scheduling line: P6 Enterprise Project Portfolio Management (EPPM), which Oracle offers on-premises or in the cloud, and the desktop P6 Professional. Oracle's documentation describes P6 Professional as designed for large-scale, multifaceted projects, with unlimited resources and target plans. Both products are documented up to version 26.
pros: Critical-path scheduling with unlimited resources and target plans (per Oracle)
Portfolio and multi-project planning in P6 EPPM
P6 EPPM runs on-premises or in Oracle's cloud
Current release (version 26) documented on docs.oracle.com
cons: No public prices: quote from Oracle or a partner
No Oman reseller confirmed in this check
Built for professional planners; a learning curve for occasional users
Scheduling only: no accounting or VAT
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public price list found.
vendors.om_specific_note: If a client or tender specifies the programme format or scheduling software, confirm the exact requirement before you buy. P6 handles scheduling only, so Oman VAT records and invoices stay in your accounting system.

vendors.name: Autodesk Forma (formerly Autodesk Construction Cloud)
vendors.tagline: Autodesk's construction platform, now sold as Autodesk Forma
vendors.market_position: Autodesk moved Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC) into its Autodesk Forma brand on 24 March 2026 and renamed the products, for example Forma Build, Forma Data Management, Forma Takeoff and Forma Estimate. Autodesk sells them in three quote-based bundles, Model Management, Preconstruction and Construction Operations, which also include Navisworks Manage, BuildingConnected Pro, ProEst and Pype tools.
pros: Model coordination, design collaboration and document management in one account
Bundles run from takeoff, estimating and bidding to field operations and closeout
User-, project- and account-based pricing options (per Autodesk)
30-day money-back guarantee stated on the pricing page
cons: No public prices for the construction bundles: quote-based
No Oman partner confirmed in this check
Product names changed in March 2026, so older guides use ACC names
Not an accounting or VAT tool
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based: Autodesk's construction pricing page lists three bundles (Model Management, Preconstruction, Construction Operations) with 'Get a quote' and no prices; Autodesk says it offers user-, project- and account-based pricing and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
vendors.om_specific_note: Most useful where a project team works from BIM models and shares drawings across companies. Ask Autodesk who resells and supports Forma in Oman before you buy, and keep Oman VAT invoicing in your accounting system.

vendors.name: Oracle Aconex
vendors.tagline: Oracle's cloud document control and project collaboration platform
vendors.market_position: Oracle Aconex is a cloud platform where every party on a project shares documents, formal correspondence (Mail) and review workflows in one auditable record; Oracle announced its purchase of Aconex in December 2017. Oracle's Aconex status page lists a Middle East (MEA) instance and a separate Saudi Arabia (KSA1) instance. Oracle announced new Aconex capabilities in April 2026.
pros: Documents, Mail and approval workflows in one shared project record
Middle East (MEA) and Saudi (KSA1) instances listed by Oracle
Oracle Aconex Mobile app for site teams
Still developed: new capabilities announced in April 2026
cons: No public prices: quote from Oracle
No Oman reseller or Oman project reference confirmed in this check
Built for multi-party projects, more than a small contractor needs
Support Central help is not offered in Arabic
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public price list found.
vendors.om_specific_note: Aconex suits main contractors, consultants and clients who need one shared record of documents and correspondence across many companies. It does not keep VAT records or issue tax invoices, so pair it with an accounting system that handles Oman VAT.

vendors.name: Procore
vendors.tagline: Construction project management, quality, safety and financials
vendors.market_position: Procore Technologies (NYSE: PCOR) sells a construction platform covering project management, quality and safety, financial management and Procore AI. It opened its first MENA office in Dubai Internet City in September 2022 and runs a UAE English site with a Dubai phone line; no Oman office, reseller or named Oman customer was found. Every contract includes unlimited users and data storage, per Procore.
pros: Unlimited users and data storage in every contract (per Procore)
Project management, quality and safety, and financial tools on one platform
500+ out-of-the-box integrations (per Procore)
24/7 support, implementation and training included in the contract (per Procore)
cons: No public prices: annual fee per product based on turnover
No Oman office, reseller or named Oman customer found
UAE site is English only, with no Arabic option
Not an accounting system: Oman VAT records stay elsewhere
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. Procore's UAE pricing page says the fee depends on the products you need and your annual turnover, with unlimited users and data storage included.
vendors.om_specific_note: Procore's nearest listed office is in Dubai and its regional site is the UAE one. For an Oman project, ask Procore who will implement and support it locally before committing, and keep Oman VAT invoicing in your accounting system.

vendors.name: Focus Softnet
vendors.tagline: ERP suite with a Muscat office and a real estate and construction edition
vendors.market_position: Focus Softnet sells the Focus X cloud ERP and related products including CRM, HCM, warehouse, POS and CAFM, plus a real estate and construction edition with project management, cost control, contract management and property management. Its Oman company, Focus Softnet LLC, has an office in MBD Business Center, Ruwi, Muscat. Focus Softnet says it has 30+ years in business, 17+ countries and 27 offices.
pros: Oman company and office in Ruwi, Muscat, with local phone lines
Project cost control, contract management and property management in one ERP
Focus says its e-invoicing is Oman-ready and Peppol compliant
Wide product range (ERP, CRM, HCM, warehouse, CAFM)
cons: No public prices: demo and quote only
A general ERP with a construction edition, not a construction-only product
OTA accreditation for e-invoicing not confirmed in this check
Broad ERP: expect an implementation project
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Focus Softnet publishes no prices and offers a demo request instead.
vendors.om_specific_note: Focus Softnet has an Oman company and a Muscat office (MBD Business Center, Ruwi), so there is a local team to ask about implementation. Its Oman site says it is 'Oman E-Invoicing Ready'; ask for proof of its Fawtara status with the Oman Tax Authority before you rely on it for e-invoicing.

vendors.name: ePROMIS
vendors.tagline: Construction and project ERP with an Oman-facing site
vendors.market_position: ePROMIS Solutions sells ERP software, including ePROMIS Construction Cloud with project management, design coordination, accounting, procurement, asset management and HR modules. It runs an Oman page aimed at contractors, but lists no Oman office address and no named Oman customer on the pages read. ePROMIS says it was established in 1981 and has over 3,000 customers worldwide.
pros: Construction Cloud built around project costs, budgets and timelines
Accounting, procurement, assets and HR in the same suite
Oman-facing site aimed at contractors
Vendor with a long history (established 1981, per ePROMIS)
cons: No public prices: demo and quote only
No Oman office address or named Oman customer found
No Oman VAT or Fawtara claims on its pages
Broad ERP: expect an implementation project
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; ePROMIS publishes no prices and offers a demo request instead.
vendors.om_specific_note: ePROMIS has an Oman page aimed at contractors, but its site lists no Oman office or Oman VAT and e-invoicing details. Ask for Oman customer references, local support arrangements and its Fawtara plan before shortlisting it.

vendors.name: Onyx Pro ERP
vendors.tagline: Arabic ERP suite with a Muscat office at Knowledge Oasis
vendors.market_position: Onyx Pro ERP is produced by Yemensoft (established 1993) and its affiliate Ultimate Solutions, and covers accounting, inventory, sales, purchasing, HR and payroll, fixed assets and a projects and progress-claims solution. Its Oman company, Ultimate Solutions for Technology LLC, has an office at Knowledge Oasis Muscat, and it lists a dealer in Salalah. Onyx says the system runs in Arabic, English, Turkish, French and German.
pros: Oman office at Knowledge Oasis Muscat, plus a Salalah dealer
Projects and progress-claims solution alongside accounting and inventory
Arabic-first, with English and other system languages (per Onyx)
Wide module range, including HR and payroll
cons: No public prices
No Oman VAT or Fawtara e-invoicing claims on its site
Website mostly in Arabic
General ERP: check contracting features in a demo
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Onyx publishes no prices.
vendors.om_specific_note: Onyx has an Oman company with an office at Knowledge Oasis Muscat (phone 24170079) and a dealer in Salalah, so local support is available to ask about. Its site does not describe Oman VAT returns or Fawtara e-invoicing, so ask for a demo of both before buying.

vendors.name: Grey ERP
vendors.tagline: Muscat-based cloud ERP with tendering and a subcontractor portal
vendors.market_position: Grey ERP is a cloud ERP with a Muscat address in Ghala Heights, linked to the Omani IT company Rawat Al Makan, which also implements Zoho, Odoo and TallyPrime. Its contracting edition lists tendering, contract and project scheduling, automated billing with progress tracking, work orders and a vendor and subcontractor portal. Grey ERP publishes no prices.
pros: Muscat office in Ghala with Omani phone lines
Tendering, contract scheduling and progress billing features
Vendor and subcontractor portal
Wider ERP modules including HR, payroll, fleet and properties
cons: No public prices: contact form only
No Fawtara e-invoicing claims on its site
No news coverage found: ask for Oman references
No BIM or critical-path scheduling features listed
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; Grey ERP publishes no prices and its 'Pricing' link opens a contact form.
vendors.om_specific_note: Grey ERP is run from Muscat (Ghala Heights), so support is local, and its contracting edition covers tendering, progress billing and a subcontractor portal. Its site mentions VAT compliance but not Fawtara e-invoicing, so ask how it will connect to the Oman Tax Authority's system.

vendors.name: Zoho (Books)
vendors.tagline: Cloud accounting with an Oman VAT edition and published USD prices
vendors.market_position: Zoho Books is cloud accounting from Zoho with an Oman edition that creates VAT invoices, applies VAT rates to sales and purchases and produces VAT reports for filing, in English or Arabic. Zoho publishes its Oman prices in US dollars, from a free plan for businesses under 50K USD revenue a year up to an Ultimate plan. It handles invoicing, bookkeeping and project time billing, not construction management.
pros: Oman edition with VAT invoices and VAT reports for filing
Published prices and a free plan
English and Arabic interface
Projects with time and expense billing
cons: Accounting, not construction management
No construction BOQ or job-costing module listed
Oman site makes no Fawtara e-invoicing claim yet
Extra users cost $2.5-$3 a month each
vendors.typical_pricing: Published in USD on Zoho's Oman site, per organisation per month, billed annually: Free $0 (revenue under 50K USD a year), Standard $15 (3 users), Professional $25 (5 users), Premium $35 (10 users), Elite $85 (10 users), Ultimate $200 (15 users). Billed monthly: $18, $30, $42, $99 and $249. Extra users $2.5 a month billed annually ($3 monthly). Prices exclude local taxes.
vendors.om_specific_note: Zoho's Oman edition handles VAT invoices and VAT reports, and its prices are shown in US dollars, not Omani rials. Oman Observer and Gulf News reported in August 2026 that e-invoicing (Fawtara) becomes mandatory in phases from April 2027; check your own start date with the Oman Tax Authority. Zoho's Oman site does not yet describe Fawtara support, so ask Zoho how it will connect before your phase starts.

vendors.name: ClearTax (Fawtara e-invoicing)
vendors.tagline: OTA-accredited Fawtara e-invoicing service provider (per ClearTax)
vendors.market_position: ClearTax, a product of Defmacro Software Pvt. Ltd., sells an e-invoicing platform for Oman's Fawtara system and says it is an OTA-accredited service provider and a Peppol-registered platform; FF News and TechAfrica reported the Oman Tax Authority accreditation in July 2026. It validates invoices against the PINT OM specification and connects to ERPs such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Xero and QuickBooks. It is a compliance layer on top of your accounting system, not accounting software.
pros: OTA-accredited service provider for Fawtara (per ClearTax and July 2026 news)
PINT OM validation and pre-transmission checks
Ready connectors for SAP, Oracle, Dynamics 365, Xero and QuickBooks
Muscat postal address listed on its Oman page
cons: No public prices: demo and quote only
Compliance layer only: you still need accounting software
Oman page offers no Arabic version
A second vendor and contract alongside your accounting software
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; ClearTax publishes no Oman prices and offers a demo booking instead.
vendors.om_specific_note: Oman is phasing in mandatory e-invoicing (Fawtara) through accredited service providers. ClearTax's page lists a pilot for the top 100 taxpayers from August 2026, businesses with annual supplies of OMR 5 million or more from April 2027 and the rest from October 2027; the Oman Tax Authority's FAQ gives different phase dates, so check your own start date with the OTA. See our Oman e-invoicing guide.

vendors.name: TallyPrime
vendors.tagline: Accounting and inventory software, sold in Oman through a Muscat dealer
vendors.market_position: TallyPrime from Tally Solutions is accounting, inventory and invoicing software, sold as Silver for a single user and Gold for multiple users on monthly, yearly or lifetime licences; Tally says 2.7M+ businesses use it. Its Middle East site covers UAE and Saudi VAT only, but Times of Oman reported a VAT-ready release for Oman in March 2021. The Muscat dealer behind tally-oman.com, Rawat Al Makan, says it configures Oman VAT invoicing and returns.
pros: Lifetime licence option as well as monthly and yearly plans
Accounting, inventory and invoicing in one package
Muscat dealer offers Oman VAT set-up, migration and training
Tally's partner locator covers Oman
cons: No Oman page or OMR prices on Tally's own site
No Fawtara e-invoicing claim found for Oman
Accounting and inventory, not construction management
Rental plans renew automatically until cancelled
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based in Oman: the Muscat dealer asks buyers to contact it for OMR prices. Tally sells TallyPrime Silver (single user) and Gold (multi-user) on 1-month, 3-month, 12-month and lifetime plans; its Middle East buy page says plans start at AED 78 but lists plan prices only in Indian rupees, with no OMR amounts.
vendors.om_specific_note: If your books already live in Tally, the Muscat dealer says it configures Oman VAT invoicing and VAT return reports. Tally's own Middle East site does not mention Oman or Fawtara, so ask the dealer how Tally will connect to Oman's e-invoicing system before your phase starts.

vendors.name: Wafeq
vendors.tagline: UAE-based cloud accounting with an Oman site and OMR pricing
vendors.market_position: Wafeq is cloud accounting software from Wafeq FZ-LLC, a UAE company, with an Oman storefront in Arabic and English and prices in OMR. It covers invoices, quotes, purchase orders, inventory, payroll and over 40 financial reports; Wafeq says more than 18,000 companies use it. Its documented e-invoicing is for Saudi Arabia's ZATCA, and its Oman pages make no claim about Oman's Fawtara e-invoicing.
pros: Published OMR prices, monthly or yearly
Arabic and English interface
Invoicing, inventory, payroll and 40+ reports in one app
14-day free trial with no card required
cons: No Oman Fawtara e-invoicing claim on its Oman pages
Contracts are with a UAE entity under Dubai (DIFC) courts
Support phone lines listed are in Dubai
Accounting software, not a construction job-costing tool
vendors.typical_pricing: Starter OMR 12/month, or OMR 10/month paid yearly (OMR 120); Plus OMR 15/month, or OMR 12/month paid yearly (OMR 150); Premium OMR 25/month, or OMR 21/month paid yearly (OMR 252); Enterprise on request, yearly only. Paid add-ons extra. No VAT note shown. 14-day free trial.
vendors.om_specific_note: Wafeq has an Oman site with Arabic and OMR pricing, but none of its Oman pages, its sitemap or its developer e-invoicing guide mention Oman's Fawtara system, which starts with 100 large taxpayers in August 2026 and reaches all remaining VAT-registered businesses in August 2027. Ask Wafeq to confirm Fawtara support before relying on it for e-invoicing.

vendors.name: Oman Tax Authority (VAT & e-invoicing)
vendors.tagline: Oman's VAT authority, running the Fawtara e-invoicing rollout from August 2026
vendors.market_position: The Oman Tax Authority administers VAT at a standard 5% rate, with first registrations effective 16 April 2021 and registration mandatory above OMR 38,500 of annual supplies. It is rolling out Fawtara e-invoicing in phases: 100 large VAT-registered companies from August 2026, all large VAT-registered companies from February 2027 and all remaining VAT-registered taxpayers, including SMEs, from August 2027.
pros: One authority for VAT, income tax and e-invoicing
Phase dates published in the Fawtara FAQ
Optional early adoption of e-invoicing allowed
Voluntary VAT registration possible from OMR 19,250
cons: VAT registration mandatory above OMR 38,500 of annual supplies
All VAT-registered businesses must e-invoice from August 2027
E-invoices must flow through an OTA-accredited service provider
Government-entity phase date not yet announced
vendors.typical_pricing: No fees are published on the Tax Authority's VAT or Fawtara pages.
vendors.om_specific_note: If your business is VAT-registered in Oman, Fawtara e-invoicing reaches you by August 2027 at the latest (Phase 3), or earlier if you are a large taxpayer. The Tax Authority uses a 5-corner model in which accredited service providers exchange invoices and report tax data to it. See our Oman e-invoicing guide.

vendors.name: Oman Society of Engineers (OSE)
vendors.tagline: Engineer accreditation needed for Oman work permits since August 2025
vendors.market_position: The Oman Society of Engineers runs a professional accreditation system in partnership with the Ministry of Labour and says accreditation is required to practise engineering in Oman. The Ministry of Labour announced in June 2025 that from 1 August 2025 engineers need this accreditation to obtain or renew a work permit. OSE grades engineers as Engineer, Associate Engineer, Professional Engineer or Consultant Engineer by degree and years of experience.
pros: Published grade fees and requirements
Online application with a stated 14-working-day review
Four grades matched to degree and experience
Oman degrees skip third-party verification
cons: Engineers cannot get or renew a work permit without it
Foreign degrees need paid third-party verification first
Grades must be renewed every 2 years
Plain OSE membership does not give a professional grade
vendors.typical_pricing: OSE lists a non-refundable OMR 35 registration fee at application; grade fees are OMR 70 (Engineer), OMR 90 (Associate Engineer), OMR 120 (Professional Engineer) and OMR 165 (Consultant Engineer), each for 2 years. Plain membership is OMR 25/year (students OMR 5).
vendors.om_specific_note: Since 1 August 2025, the Ministry of Labour requires engineers in Oman to hold OSE accreditation before a work permit is issued or renewed. For engineers with degrees from outside Oman, allow time for degree verification (OSE quotes up to 21 working days or more) plus the 14-working-day OSE review.

vendors.name: Authority for Projects, Tenders & Local Content
vendors.tagline: Oman's public-procurement authority and Esnad contractor registration
vendors.market_position: Royal Decree 57/2025 of 24 June 2025 turned the Secretariat General of the Tender Board into the Authority for Projects, Tenders and Local Content, an independent body under the Council of Ministers. It runs the Esnad eTendering portal, where suppliers, contractors and consulting offices register and are classified, and it sets local-content targets and reviews government contracts above OMR 3 million before signing.
pros: One online portal (Esnad) for registration, classification and tenders
Registration rules and regulations published on its site
Esnad mobile apps for Android and iOS
Classification can be upgraded as the company grows
cons: Registration and classification needed to bid for government work
Certificates must be renewed and data kept up to date
Local-content rules include a mandatory list of goods, services and jobs
Registration fees not shown on the pages checked
vendors.typical_pricing: No registration or classification fees are published on the Authority's site pages checked.
vendors.om_specific_note: Use the current name: the Authority for Projects, Tenders and Local Content (Royal Decree 57/2025), not the Tender Board. To bid on government work, register and get classified on its Esnad portal (etendering.tenderboard.gov.om), and check its mandatory local-content list of goods, services and jobs.

vendors.name: Ministry of Labour / Omanisation
vendors.tagline: Oman's labour ministry: work permits and Omanisation targets
vendors.market_position: The Ministry of Labour issues and renews work permits for non-Omani staff and enforces Omanisation targets. Under Ministerial Decision 602/2025, in force since late January 2026, firms are sorted into green, yellow and red categories by Omanisation compliance: green firms get a 30% discount on visa and licensing fees, while yellow and red firms pay double, according to Muscat Daily. Some professions are closed to non-Omanis, and since 1 August 2025 engineers need professional accreditation for a work permit.
pros: Work permits issued and renewed online
30% fee discount for firms meeting Omanisation targets
Free self-service Omanisation compliance certificate
Training contract and wage support services for hiring Omanis
cons: Firms missing Omanisation targets pay double permit fees
Some professions are closed to non-Omanis
Every private firm must employ at least one Omani
Engineers need OSE accreditation for a work permit
vendors.typical_pricing: The ministry lists a service fee of OMR 301 for issuing or renewing an establishment's work permit for a non-Omani worker (individual employers: OMR 101 to issue, OMR 141 to renew). Since January 2026 firms meeting Omanisation targets get 30% off and firms falling short pay double, per Muscat Daily's report of Decision 602/2025.
vendors.om_specific_note: No single construction-wide Omanisation percentage was found in this check. What matters now is your firm's green, yellow or red category under Decision 602/2025, which moves work permit and visa fees 30% down or doubles them, and the list of professions closed to non-Omanis. Check your standing in the ministry's e-services before pricing expat-heavy work.

vendors.name: Muscat Municipality (Building Permits)
vendors.tagline: Building permits for Muscat through municipal e-services
vendors.market_position: Muscat Municipality issues building permits in Muscat governorate. Its e-services portal lists building licences, technical licences and building completion certificates, and its Baladiyeti app (updated November 2025) handles building permit renewal and municipal licence renewal.
pros: Building licences handled on the e-services portal
Baladiyeti app for permit renewals and service requests
Online payment through the e-services portal
Minor-works permits for extensions and modifications
cons: Permit fees not published on the pages checked
Covers Muscat governorate only
Completion certificate needed after building
Main website is script-heavy and hard to read
vendors.typical_pricing: No building permit fees are published on the Muscat Municipality pages checked.
vendors.om_specific_note: In Muscat, apply for building permits and completion certificates through the municipality's e-services portal (eservices.mm.gov.om); the Baladiyeti app covers renewals. Outside Muscat governorate, check with the local municipality. Build permit lead time into the programme.

vendors.name: Oman Building Code (MoHUP)
vendors.tagline: Oman's unified building code, optional now and mandatory by 2030
vendors.market_position: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Planning unveiled a unified Oman building code in October 2025, developed with the International Code Council under a March 2024 agreement that covered six codes. According to Muscat Daily, use is optional in 2026 and 2027, enforcement starts in Muscat governorate in 2028 and reaches all governorates by 2030. It applies to new buildings, and to existing ones only on major renovation or expansion.
pros: One national code in place of differing local rules
Two optional years (2026-2027) to train and adapt
Existing buildings exempt unless majorly renovated or expanded
Separate guide for work on historic buildings
cons: Mandatory for new Muscat projects from 2028
Mandatory nationwide by 2030
Design and site teams must learn the new code
Enforcement dates differ by governorate until 2030
vendors.typical_pricing: No official fees found in the sources checked.
vendors.om_specific_note: The unified building code is being phased in: optional in 2026 and 2027, enforced in Muscat from 2028 and nationwide by 2030, for new construction. Projects designed now for completion after 2028 in Muscat should be checked against it.

vendors.name: Civil Defence & Ambulance Authority (CDAA)
vendors.tagline: Oman's civil defence authority setting building fire-safety rules
vendors.market_position: The Civil Defence and Ambulance Authority took its current name under Royal Decree 39/2021, replacing the Public Authority for Civil Defence and Ambulance. Its responsibilities include setting the civil-defence safety conditions that buildings and facilities must meet, issuing the related licences and monitoring compliance. Its services include studying construction plans and projects, stating their safety requirements and following up on implementation.
pros: One national authority for building fire-safety requirements
Reviews construction plans and states safety requirements
Publishes awareness and civil-protection guidance
Laws and royal decrees listed on its website
cons: Fire-safety requirements must be met in design and construction
Field inspections of residential, commercial and industrial premises
No fees or approval steps published online
No e-service link found on its website
vendors.typical_pricing: No fees are published on the Civil Defence and Ambulance Authority's website.
vendors.om_specific_note: Use the current name, Civil Defence and Ambulance Authority (CDAA), in place of the pre-2021 Public Authority for Civil Defence and Ambulance. CDAA studies construction plans and states their fire-safety requirements, so bring its requirements into the design stage.

vendors.name: GIG Insurance Oman (GIG Gulf)
vendors.tagline: Engineering insurance for contractors from GIG Gulf, formerly AXA Gulf
vendors.market_position: GIG Gulf is the former AXA Gulf business, bought by Kuwait's Gulf Insurance Group in 2021; Canada's Fairfax Financial lists Gulf Insurance Group among its insurance companies. Its Oman site lists contractors all-risk (from villas to bridges), erection all-risk, contractor's plant and machinery, machinery breakdown and electronic equipment cover, sold project by project or as an annual multi-project policy. GIG Gulf says it has a specialised team of engineers to help with risk management.
pros: Full engineering range: CAR, EAR, plant, machinery, electronic equipment
Annual policy option covering multiple projects
In-house engineering team for risk management (GIG Gulf says)
Oman toll-free line 800 70 292
cons: No published rates
Product page gives cover names, not limits or exclusions
No online quote price shown for engineering cover
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates.
vendors.om_specific_note: GIG Gulf is the renamed AXA Gulf business, which Gulf Insurance Group bought in 2021. Ask whether an annual multi-project CAR policy suits your workload better than insuring each project separately.

vendors.name: Liva Insurance (Oman)
vendors.tagline: Omani insurer formed from NLGIC and Al Ahlia, writing contractors all-risk cover
vendors.market_position: Liva Insurance SAOC is the Oman company of the Liva brand, which NLGIC and RSA Middle East adopted in 2023 after NLGIC bought RSA Middle East in 2022. Liva says its business comes from integrating NLGIC and Al Ahlia Insurance and that it serves over 1.5 million customers across Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, the UAE and Oman. Its Oman product list includes contractors all-risk, contractor plant and machinery, machinery insurance case by case, and workmen's compensation.
pros: Contractors all-risk and contractor plant and machinery cover
Workmen's compensation from the same insurer
Fire, marine cargo and motor fleet cover for trade firms
Operates in five GCC markets
cons: No Erection All Risk product listed online
Machinery cover only case by case
No published rates
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates.
vendors.om_specific_note: Liva says it was formed by integrating NLGIC and Al Ahlia Insurance, two names Omani contractors may know from older policies. Its online list has CAR but no erection all-risk, so ask directly if you install plant or equipment.

vendors.name: Oman United Insurance (OUIC)
vendors.tagline: Omani listed insurer with published CAR and EAR cover details
vendors.market_position: Oman United Insurance Company SAOG is listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange and says it has operated in Oman for over 35 years. Its project-insurance page sets out contractors all-risk and erection all-risk cover in detail: material damage and public liability sections, maintenance cover up to 12 months after completion, a testing and commissioning period for EAR, and optional extensions such as debris removal, professional fees and the principal's existing property.
pros: CAR and EAR sections, extensions and exclusions published online
Maintenance cover up to 12 months after completion
Optional debris removal, professional fees and principal's property
Listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange
cons: Operates in Oman only
No published rates
Excludes consequential loss and pandemic-related loss
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published rates.
vendors.om_specific_note: Oman United publishes its CAR and EAR cover structure, extensions and exclusions online, which makes it easy to compare against other quotes before you ask for one.

vendors.name: ProTenders
vendors.tagline: GCC construction project intelligence and eTendering, with a free company profile
vendors.market_position: ProTenders, operated by NuServ Ltd and started in 2011 according to its about page, combines a free company-profile directory, a paid construction-intelligence database and an eTendering tool. It sells the intelligence product as covering projects from planning to completion across the GCC and has an Oman projects page. It is business-to-business project tracking for developers, consultants, contractors and suppliers, not a homeowner job marketplace.
pros: Free company profile that can bid on private tenders
Tracks GCC projects, including Oman, from planning to completion
Paid tier lists project participants and sends notifications
eTendering tool for running your own tenders
cons: Intelligence and eTendering are custom-priced
Project data needs sign-up or login
No office in Oman listed (Abu Dhabi and Montreal)
vendors.typical_pricing: Company Profiles free; Construction Intelligence and Construction eTendering are custom-priced after a demo request, with no published figures.
vendors.om_specific_note: ProTenders has an Oman projects page and its paid intelligence covers GCC projects from planning to completion, so an Omani contractor or supplier can use it to find private-sector project leads. The free profile lets you bid on private tenders; Omani government tenders run separately on the Esnad portal.
